The implementation is complete, clean, and passing all tests. Here's a summary of the work:

## Summary

I built a complete RS274/NGC G-code simulator in JavaScript (Node.js 22+, stdlib only) at `output/main.js` with 15 supporting modules in `output/lib/`.

**Process**: Read the full 5,862-line spec and clarifications, designed the architecture (all motion computed in absolute/R-space with derived work-coordinates, a "path" abstraction shared by straight/arc/compound-CRC moves, and a diff-based trace recorder that automatically handles delta-encoding and the tricky "trailing entry at same timestamp" case), then implemented the parser, expression evaluator, order-of-execution engine, motion/arc math, canned cycles (G81–G89), cutter radius compensation (Appendix B), and the trace sampling engine (time/distance/tolerance-adaptive).

**Validation**: Matched all 3 worked trace examples in the spec exactly, all values in the spec's own expression test program (Appendix C.2), the full canned-cycle test program (Appendix C.3) across all three planes, and the "Hello World" sample (Appendix C.1). Hand-derived and verified cutter-comp entry moves, corner convexity, arc handedness in all three planes, G84's spindle trailing-entry mechanism, G28/G30/G92 family, and dozens of error conditions.

**Bugs found and fixed** (via self-review, an independent review subagent, and continued testing):
1. Canned-cycle incremental-mode depth was computed from the wrong base position (must be R, not pre-cycle position — caught by re-testing against the spec's own §3.5.16.2 Example 2)

3. G93 (inverse-time) didn't require F on every motion line
4. Missing `--tool-table`/`--parameter-input` files incorrectly caused exit 2 instead of exit 1
5. Negative tool-table diameters didn't flip the compensation side (Appendix B.4)
